questions.stemHtml: A particle moves along the $x$-axis so that at time $t \ge 0$ its velocity is modeled by the differentiable function $$v(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9.$$ At $t = 0$, the particle is located at position $x = 2$.
questions.promptHtml: What is the position of the particle at time $t = 2$?

questions.stemHtml: Consider the continuous function $f$ defined by $f(x) = \ln(x^2 + 1)$ for all real numbers $x$.
Suppose the Maclaurin series for a smooth function $g$ centered at $x = 0$ is given by $$g(x) = 1 + 2x + \frac{3}{2}x^2 + \frac{2}{3}x^3 + \cdots$$
questions.promptHtml: What is the value of the third derivative $g'''(0)$?

explanations.2: By the chain rule, $$f'(x) = \frac{2x}{x^2 + 1}.$$ Evaluating at $x = 1$ gives $f'(1) = \frac{2(1)}{1 + 1} = 1$.
explanations.3: The coefficient of $x^3$ in a Maclaurin series is $\frac{g'''(0)}{3!}$. Setting $\frac{g'''(0)}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$ gives $g'''(0) = 4$.

frqQuestions.stemHtml: Let $y = f(x)$ be the solution to the separable differential equation $$\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x(y - 1)$$ with initial condition $f(0) = 3$.
frqQuestions.promptHtml:
(a) Write an equation for the tangent line to the graph of $y = f(x)$ at $x = 0$, and use it to approximate $f(0.1)$.

(b) Solve the differential equation for $y = f(x)$.
frqQuestions.rubricHtml:
• Point 1: Slope at $(0,3)$ is $2(0)(2)=0$, so tangent line is $y = 3$ and $f(0.1) \approx 3$.
  • Point 2: Separates variables as $\frac{1}{y-1}\,dy = 2x\,dx$ and integrates to $\ln|y-1| = x^2 + C$.
  • Point 3: Applies $f(0)=3$ to find $y = 1 + 2e^{x^2}$.
